records.remarks: • MSP partial shutdown: While testing MSP TG 3 starter motor from VFD, heavy earth fault occurred on VFD and starter module leading to tripping of MSP Emergency bus incomer breaker. Due to tripping of main breaker, UPS failed to provide power from battery back-up leading to tripping of UPS power at MSP. Due to this, all PLC panels and DCS powered off leading to tripping of both MSP TGs, both MSP PGCs and all four BGCs at 1945 hrs. BHS PGC-A also tripped in cascading at same time. After loading MSP TG-1, 2, BGC-C and BHS PGC-A loaded at 2140 hrs and 2210 hrs respectively. BGC-C again tripped due to suction KOD level hihi at 2215 hrs leading to tripping of MSP TG-1 &2 due to hunting. Subsequently, HSW MIP 1210, 1240 & 1250 tripped in load shedding.MSP PGC-A, B and 04 BGCs loaded by 0005 hrs and 0235 hrs respectively. All HSW MIP-1210, MIP-1240, MIP-1250 started by 0245 hrs. During revival, Lift gas pressure significantly down up to 47 ksc for around 6 hrs. (Oil loss: 280 bbls, Gas loss: 0.454 mmscm, HSW loss: 40800 bbls)
records.short_remarks: • MSP partial shutdown: While testing MSP TG 3 starter motor from VFD, heavy earth fault occurred on VFD and starter module leading to tripping of MSP Emergency bus incomer breaker

Well head team mobilised. Observed total shutdown due to low pneumatic signal in SDP-100. Also observed leakage from downstream flange of bean housing of #2. So replaced the ring gasket of the leaking flange joint of #2 Bean housing. While pressure testing the PFA, again found leakage from the same flange joint. Upon inspection, found PFA side flange groove damaged. Hence PFA spool removed for flange replacement and installed 8"#900 Blind flange to isolate PFA of #2. SDP charging in progress. Other wells could not be revived early due to passing of all group header valves. To makeup gas deficiency choke stepped up of WO16#6 from 40/64” to 56/64” and choke stepped up of WO16#7 from 32/64” to 48/64” B-119#1,#3, #4,#5 opened by 1930 hrs except B-119#2 after removal of PFA of #2. Platform normalized. Oil loss: 400 bbls, Gas loss: 0.97 MMSCMD.

records.remarks: • 18" RS-15—>SHG WFL leakage rectification job by SEAMEC-II: 18" RS-15—>SHG WFL leakage rectification job by SEAMEC-II:  (Oil loss: 961 BOPD, Gas loss: 0.454 MMSCMD) At 2200 hrs(30.08.2026), Well #3 of RS‑15 was opened following completion of the 18" RS‑15 to SHG WFL leakage rectification job executed by Seamec‑II. However, at 0300(31.08.2026) hrs high‑intensity gas bubbles were observed approximately 10–15 meters east of the RS‑15 platform. The matter was immediately conveyed to Seamec‑II, but the vessel reported its inability to carry out the survey as it had been de‑hired and will be moving to Mumbai post derigging. As a precautionary measure, all RS‑15 wells have been kept closed, and waiting for the arrival of the IMR vessel for further inspection and rectification. Max pressure during the entire operation was 14 ksc at RS-15 end.

records.remarks: • MSP : Observed steam coming from MSP hot oil expansion tank due to ingress of water in hot oil system. Suspected shell and tube communication from MSP E-3180 heater or cooling water communication in hot oil pump. Isolated the heater E-3180. (Oil loss 590 bbls, Gas loss 0.389  MMSCM), Due to the unavailability of a heat sink, the hot oil temperature approached critical limits, due to MSP PGC-A, PGC-B, TG-1,TG-2 WHRU passing. To  safeguard the system, stopped MSP PGC-A, MSP PGC-B, and MSP TG-2 at 1700 hrs. Stopped BGC-B and BGC-D for power management. During this period MLGIP down by 20ksc. IA#2,5,11, RS-4#6, RS-1#2 were closed from RPMC at 1830 hrs to avoid gas flaring and to maintain MLGIP. IF#2,IP#2,4(S1 gas) closed to avoid flaring. BHS separators V-210 and V-220 taken in pressurized mode at 1700 hrs and 2200 hrs respectively due to non availablity of 02 BGC. Loaded MSP PGC-B at 2230 hrs. Observed dense fumes again from MSP Hot oil expansion tank,  To safeguard the system, stopped hot oil pump P-4545 at 0430 hrs and MSP PGC-B at 0445 hrs respectively.
records.short_remarks: • MSP: Observed steam coming from MSP hot oil expansion tank due to ingress of water in hot oil system; IA#2, RS-4#6, RS-1#2 closed

records.remarks: • ED/RS-7: Gas bubbles near the ED jacket. OSV AM Phoenix was deployed for verification and confirmed gas bubbles at coordinates 19°18.560' N, 071°26.201' E. MSV Seamec Agastya reported at ED @0930 Hrs on 03.11.2026 for identification and rectification of leakage from 12" ED - SHG MWFL. Initial Survey carried out by Diver and reported 1 leakage above J-tube in 12" ED - SHG MWFL. Closed all wells of RS-7 and ED platform from 1215 hrs to 1250 hrs on 03.11.2026 (as RS-7 flows through ED platforms). Diver found approx. 1650 mm long damaged section of concrete coating at 3o/c position at J tube. Confirmed at leak location 1 - 02 holes were located both at 6o/c position. Leakages rectified by installing 6 clamps (3 nos of 200 mm and 3 nos of 100 mm). Wells opening of RS-7 and ED started at 1140 hrs, observed another pin hole leakage (Leak hole 3- 2mm x 3mm) between 20 mm gap between clamp-5 and clamp-6. Again closed wells at 1240 hrs for rectification. Installed the newly fabricated clamp 200 mm long at leak hole 3 and rectified leakage. Started wells opening slowly at 2100 hrs by maintaining MLP below 11.5 ksc at the ED end of 12"" ED-SHG WFL due to fragile line condition. All wells of ED and RS-7 platform opened by 0400 hrs.(Oil & Gas loss : 790 Bbls & 0.503mmscm).
